conventions.convention: F₂ denotes the two residue classes modulo 2 with quotient addition and multiplication; this item does not assert the field axioms.
The binary dot product is the left-to-right XOR fold of coordinatewise conjunctions, with empty fold 0 and n ≥ 0.

The standard query acts on address followed by target, preserves the address, and XORs a total function value into an arbitrary target. Address and target widths may be zero. One invocation is one query, separately from elementary gate costs.
The Boolean phase query is P_f|x⟩ = (−1)^{f(x)}|x⟩. Its access contract supplies uncontrolled access only; controlled access requires a separate promise.
The reversible dot-product procedure uses one distinct zero-initialized work bit and callable Toffoli and CNOT gates, counts each occurrence once, and makes no oracle calls.
Preparing the kickback target from zero applies X first and H second, yielding |−⟩. The conversion leaves that target in |−⟩ and counts two preparation gates.
For reverse conversion, the output qubit is the first, control register of C(P_f); Hadamards act on that output before and after the explicitly supplied controlled call.

load_bearing.statement: For a total function f:{0,1}^a → {0,1}^b with a,b ≥ 0, U_f|x⟩|y⟩ = |x⟩|y ⊕ f(x)⟩. The map is an involution and is unitary; no injectivity is assumed.
For a Boolean function f:{0,1}^a → {0,1}, P_f|x⟩ = (−1)^{f(x)}|x⟩. This definition supplies uncontrolled access only; controlled access is a separate promise.
For every total Boolean f, U_f(|x⟩|−⟩) = (−1)^{f(x)}|x⟩|−⟩. Thus the address acquires exactly P_f, the target returns unchanged, and the same identity holds for every address superposition.
For n ≥ 0 and a,x ∈ {0,1}^n, a·x is the left-to-right XOR fold of a_i ∧ x_i, with empty fold 0; its residue class is the sum of the coordinate products modulo 2.

For every n ≥ 0, the algorithm maps |a⟩|x⟩|z⟩|0⟩_r to |a⟩|x⟩|z ⊕ (a·x)⟩|0⟩_r, extends linearly to superpositions, and uses exactly 2n Toffoli gates, one CNOT, and one clean work bit, with no failure branch.

For constant Boolean f with value c, P_f = (−1)^c I and a standalone call preserves every pure-state measurement law. Explicit controlled phase access distinguishes c=0 from c=1 with certainty using a |+⟩ control and measurement in the {|+⟩,|−⟩} basis.

published_dependencies.used_for: Congruence modulo 2 means divisibility of the difference; used to verify the two residue classes and their distinction.
Defines the quotient carrier and identifies equality of residue classes with congruence of representatives.
Supplies representative-independent quotient addition and multiplication, specialized to modulus 2 for XOR, conjunction, and the parity sum.

seams_checked.note: Total address functions, instance promises, zero initialization, and separate query and nonoracle gate costs are preserved.
Clean-work restoration and XOR involutivity match the suppliers. The Boolean-DAG bound is quoted as 6S+4E+b gates and S+E work bits without applying compute-copy-uncompute a second time.
Ket notation and the root linear-first inner-product convention are used consistently; the calculations introduce no conjugation discrepancy.
Ordered computational bases and linear extension are used within their stated domains, including the one-dimensional zero-qubit register.
Control-first blocks, separately granted controlled and inverse access, and the distinction between global and controlled relative phase are preserved.
The normalized |−⟩ target is used as a pure-state representative; no additional preparation capability follows from the pure-state definition.
Exact H and X matrices give HX|0⟩=|−⟩ and H diag(1,−1) H=X. Callable-gate assumptions are stated separately.
Gate occurrences, chronological inverse circuits, workspace, and query charges retain the supplier resource conventions.
The cited parity definition and kickback identity agree with the suppliers; the exact-query procedures explicitly prepare their response with X followed by H.
Consumers use the total multi-output XOR query and parity dot product. Field properties have a separate field theorem rather than being inferred from the residue-carrier definition.
The phase mark uses one ordinary XOR call with an explicitly prepared |−⟩ response; candidate verification is charged separately.
Counting explicitly requires controlled membership-reflection access and distinguishes controlled powers from repeated controlled calls. It does not infer either from a bare phase oracle.
The XOR action and involution are preserved. The model explicitly distinguishes binary addresses from its general N-level address-register extension.
The one-hot address function is explicitly completed to a total Boolean function, including N=0, before invoking the standard XOR query.
The finite address model uses the same XOR basis action and involution. Controlled consistency reflection uses two unconditional XOR calls and does not assume controlled unknown-oracle access.
